topic.title: Project Review Tasks Page
topic.shortdesc: The Project Review Tasks page allows you to manage review tasks, create new tasks, and integrate reviewed changes into the project.

body.p: A Project Review Task is a review task created from content in a Content Fusion project. It is part of the project workflow and allows accepted changes to be integrated back into the project content.

section.title: Project Review Tasks Page
section.p: The Project Review Tasks page lists all current tasks created in the current project.
Tasks created within a project differ slightly from regular tasks created outside a project:

ul.li: A project-based review task is created from the Content Fusion browser interface within a project, whereas a regular review task is created from Oxygen XML Editor/Author or the browser interface outside a project.

Changes made to a project-based review task are stored in the project's Git repository. When the task is finished, they are merged into the project's default branch and pushed to the upstream remote repository.
All the authors that have access to a project will be able to see all review tasks created in that project.
A project-based review task contains all the files in the project (not just the files selected for review).

section.p: To open an existing task, click it. This opens the Task Files page.
You can use the Filter by name field to filter the list of review tasks, making it easier to find specific tasks.

To see tasks that you created (or are assigned as an owner), click the Owned By Me tab. To see tasks that have been assigned to you, click the Assigned To Me tab. The table also has columns that show project information (if applicable), the Owners of the review task, the review status, and the Due Date (if specified in the Task Settings page).

A task is displayed as In review unless it is closed by a task owner. If a task has been closed, the status is displayed as Review closed. Other task statuses that a task owner can see are Integrating and Integrated (see the section below).
Integrated tasks are not displayed by default. To view all tasks, click the Show integrated button (when inside the Owned By Me tab). To hide them, click the same button again.
The Show Only for Current Branch button filters the task list to show only review tasks for the current branch.

For tasks in the Owned By Me tab, if you hover over the task, a vertical ellipsis () becomes available on the far right side. This opens an actions menu that includes a Delete action that can be used to delete the review task.

section.title: Review Tasks Header
section.p: When a review task is open, the upper part of the header stripe remains the same regardless of which page you navigate to within the task. This makes certain navigation options and the breadcrumb available at all times.

fig.title: Review Tasks Header Stripe (Within a Project)

section.p: The bottom part of the header stripe changes depending on the context and user role. It contains helpful information and actions. It shows the task title, review status, information about task owners, the number of reviewers who have finalized the task, and the due date, if one is specified in the Task Settings page. Click the More Details button to view information such as the creation time and current branch, if the task is in a project.
If you are the owner of the task, the Share button is available to open a dialog box where you can configure share settings.

Click the Owners area to view a pop-up box with information about task owners. For any accessible review task that originates from a project, if you are not already an Owner, you can click Assign Me as Owner to become an Owner.
For any review task that you are assigned as a task owner, you can click the Add owner action to open the Sharing Settings window where you can assign an additional owner to the task.
You can click on the Finalized widget (drop-down) to see the status for each assigned reviewer:

The task owner has access to several actions in the Review Status box:
Add reviewers - Opens the Sharing Settings window where you can add additional reviewers.
Request re-review - Use this action for a task whose reviewers have finalized their review. It resets the finalized status for all reviewers and changes their status to In progress. Also, if the task owner reopens a closed task, the finalized status is reset for all reviewers.

Any users who have been assigned to the task but have not yet accessed it are labeled as Pending in the Review Status Summary pop-up window so that task owners can identify users who have ignored the review request.

When a reviewer opens a task that the owner requested that they do another review, the Task Files page includes a Changed files only filter option to make it easy to identify which files have changes that need to be reviewed again.

section.title: Creating New Tasks and Files Within a Project
section.p:
To create a new task and add files:
From the Review Tasks page, click the New Task button.
Enter a task title in the field at the top of the pane. When you are finished, click the check mark on the right.
Optionally, specify a Due Date. The time remaining until the due date is displayed under the review task title when you navigate within the task and in the table on the My Review Tasks page. Also, reviewers who have not finalized the task receive an email notification when the due date is within 3 days, 1 day, and 12 hours of its expiration.
Optionally, you can enter a Description for the task.
To add files to the task, select the file from the Files side-pane.If you want to create a new file to add to the task (or upload an existing one from your computer), you will first need to finish creating the task. After clicking the Create button, the Task Files page for the review task should be open. On this page, you can create or upload files to the task. To create a new file, click the New File button and you will be able to choose a file type from a list of templates, then choose a file name in the text field at the bottom, and click OK. You can then open the file in the visual editor page to make changes to the document. To upload a file, click the Upload button and select the file from your computer.
Optionally, you can select a Context Publication (the publication must already be defined in the ). The benefit of specifying a context publication is that the files added to the task will be rendered as a hierarchical tree based upon the context DITA map defined in the publication.
Optionally, select Settings from the left stripe to open the Task Settings page to configure options or delete the task.
Click Create to finish the task creation process.
The next logical step would most likely be to share the task with anyone you want to review the documents.

section.title: Closing a Review Task and Integrating Changes
section.p: A task owner can close the review process to allow time to address feedback and integrate changes. To close a task, click the Close review button in the top stripe while a task is open. This locks the task and prevents others from making changes to it. If further review is needed, click the Reopen review button to make the task editable again.

The Start integration button opens a built-in file comparison and merge tool. You can use it to view differences, choose which differences to copy to your local version, and merge the differences. The task status changes to Integrating during this process.

Once in the Integrating status, only the author who initiated the integration can work on integrating the task. As the initiating author, you can use the Cancel integration button to abandon the integration (for example, to allow another author to start the integration).
After resolving the differences, use Finish integration.
If you have write access to the project, this drop-down menu offers two actions:

ul.li: Integrate on [the originating Git branch] - Commits the resolved review to that branch and sets the task status to Integrated. This action cannot be undone.

Integrate in workspace - Adds the resolved review to your personal workspace as uncommitted changes, then sets the task status to Integrated. Your workspace must be clean first, with no uncommitted changes. You can then edit the files in the workspace and commit them to the project when you are ready. If you have write access to the project, you can use Mark as not integrated to return the task to Review closed.

section.p: If you started the integration but only collaborate on the project, the button is Integrate in workspace, not Finish integration.
